subject: Inference economics: batching/quantization openness + next steps
messages:
From: Sylvia Park <sylvia@noblefin.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Torres <alex.torres@noblefin.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up: inference cost drivers & pilot criteria

Hi Naomi / Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — it was helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our side so we can pull together a pilot ask for procurement:

- High-level cost pressure: we're seeing ~35% QoQ growth in model usage across our fraud-detection and customer-support flows. Unit economics are the gating factor for scaling.
- Current stack: mostly hosted endpoints on a managed GPU provider (NVIDIA A100 instances), model is a fine-tuned 7B transformer; we do some ad-hoc caching at proxy layer but nothing centralized or token-aware.
- Success criteria for pilot: 40% or greater reduction in per-inference cost (tokens + infra) at P95 latency <= 450ms for our typical 350-token requests.

Specific asks:
1) Can you share typical batching/latency tradeoffs for a 7B-class model under continuous batching (10-50 QPS range)?
2) Are there quantized variants you recommend that preserve quality for classification/rerank tasks? What's the usual quality delta you observe (accuracy/F1)?
3) We can share a small sample of request token distributions — would that be useful to get more concrete cost estimates?

We're trying to make a decision on a Reserved/Dedicated pilot vs. sticking with our current managed GPUs. Procurement wants a clear expected unit cost range and SLOs to compare.

Attaching a small workload-sample.csv with anonymized request sizes.

Thanks,
Sylvia Park
Head of Platform
NobleFin

Attachments: workload-sample.csv (attachment)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up: inference cost drivers & pilot criteria

Sylvia — thanks for the clear asks and for the sample. Short recap from our side and proposed next steps so procurement can see concrete items: 

Recap of pain and goals (as I understand them):
- Pain: unit costs growing fast as usage scales; current setup has limited token-aware caching and no quantization in prod.
- Goal: reduce per-inference dollar cost by ~40% while keeping P95 latency <= 450ms and no more than a 1-2% drop in classification F1.

What we heard re current infra: 7B fine-tuned model, A100 instances, proxy-level caching only, QPS in the 10-50 range. Correct me if anything above is off.

What Redwood can do and initial signals:
- Batching & latency: for 7B models we typically see cost/throughput improvements with continuous batching up to 2.5–3x in token throughput when QPS is steady; P95 latency depends on batching window and concurrency. For a 350-token request at 20 QPS, a tuned continuous-batching profile often hits ~300–420ms P95 on dedicated T4x8 / A10 pools; on shared hosted tiers P95 is higher.
- Caching expectations: prefix/KV caching yields biggest wins for repeated contexts (e.g., rerank or multi-turn sessions). If ~25–30% of token stream is repeated across requests, effective token compute can drop substantially.
- Quantization: we support int8/int4 variants and fused kernels. For classification/rerank tasks we've seen minimal quality drop (<=1–2% relative F1) with 8-bit and acceptable tradeoffs at 4-bit depending on the model fine-tuning. We'll validate on your sample.
- Unit cost framing: we'll provide an expected per-1k-token cost range across three configs: Hosted-optimized (default kernels + opportunistic batching), Dedicated-reserved (pinned GPU pools, tuned kernels + autoscale), and Private (VPC, customer-managed infra + Redwood runtime).

Concrete next steps (proposed timeline):
1) We (Redwood) run a lightweight cost sensitivity run against your sample (token histogram + 2000 representative requests) — deliverable: per-config unit cost range + latency envelope. (Need your confirmed sample and a short notes doc describing representative traffic patterns) — 3 business days after sample.
2) Joint sync to review results and alignment on SLA/discounts for a Reserved pilot — 30–45 minute call.
3) If results look good, we scope a 6-week pilot: ingestion of a production-like workload, 1 or 2 quantization trials, and a caching/batching config test. Procurement will need expected cost delta and the plan for fallback to your current endpoints.

Questions for you:
- Can you share the sample as CSV + a short doc describing what fraction of requests are single-turn vs multi-turn, and which endpoints are highest volume?
- Any non-negotiable latency targets (other than the P95 450ms stated)?
- Are there data residency/compliance constraints we should flag for Private deployment?

I'll follow up with a short proposal doc and timeframe. Rishi / Monica — looping you in for ops/quantization guidance and pilot scoping.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com

Naomi / team — thanks for the quick recap and proposed steps. Confirming: we'll send the expanded sample today (CSV + short doc on single vs multi-turn fractions) and the procurement team requested a high-level SLA request (attached).

Two quick clarifications:
- On the latency bullet: the P95 450ms is a firm goal for our live fraud flow; customer-support flows can tolerate up to 800ms at P95.
- On quantization: procurement wants an explicit statement about fallbacks if a quantized variant shows a >2% F1 drop in production. Is that typically covered in your pilot plan?

We are available for a 30-minute sync tomorrow 10:00–11:30 PT if that works on your side.
